newsitem.title: UK: Women to gain most from British minimum wage.
newsitem.headline: Women to gain most from British minimum wage.

text.p: British working women stand to gain most when the new Labour government fulfils its pledge to introduce a minimum wage, a report said on Friday.

"The Labour government's commitment to a national minimum wage is good news for women who face a greater risk than men of low pay," said Gary Bowker, co-editor of the Equal Opportunities Review which published the report.
The report showed that over three million UK female employees and over 1.5 million male employees would benefit from a national minimum wage set at four pounds an hour.

Figures from a Labour Force survey show employees in the UK earn on average 7.36 pounds an hour but many come nowhere near that level with almost one million UK employees earning less than 2.50 pounds an hour and around 20 percent on less than four pounds an hour.
Despite closer ties between unions and business leaders, the two remain at odds over the level of the minimum wage.
Britain's second largest union, the Transport and General Workers, on Tuesday called for the wage to be set at four pounds an hour, but business groups have recommended a figure below 3.50 pounds.
The report analysed the impact of a minimum wage set at five levels from 4.50 pounds down to 2.50. In all cases women stood to gain more than their male colleagues.
"Women employees are almost twice as likely to be low-paid than male employees," the report said.
Britain's part-time workers would also benefit disproportionately. Part-time work accounts for 44 percent of female employment.

A recent paper published by Susan Harkness at the London School of Economics found that income from women's work had become more important to families in the UK and was crucial for keeping many of them above the poverty line.
"Women's earnings now form an increasingly large component of total family income," the paper said. "Women's pay, despite being low, plays a critical role in preventing poverty."
But Bowker at the Equal Opportunities Review called on the government to go further and strengthen current equal pay legislation.

"Minimum wage protection, though a necessary element in any equal pay strategy, is not sufficient on its own to significantly narrow the pay inequality gap. It needs to be complemented by strong and effective equal legislation," he said.

Britain's ethnic population also stands to gain from the minimum wage. Ethnic minority groups are marginally more likely than white employees to be earning less than four pounds an hour, the report said.
Labour on Wednesday pledged to introduce a minimum wage set according to the economic circumstances of the time and taking into account the advice of an independent Low Pay Commission.
